description: Server package + demo page: full implementation of all five packages/server/src/ files (types, knowledge, train, chat, index) plus demo/index.html and README.md. Depends on FEAT-001 (deps installed) and FEAT-002 (widget dist/pluggable-bot.js built, so server can embed it). The widget JS is inlined into the Worker bundle at build time by reading dist/pluggable-bot.js in a wrangler plugin or by embedding it as a base64/raw string import — use the raw string approach: in index.ts, import the widget JS as text using a ?raw import (wrangler supports this via a text_blob binding) OR simply serve the built file from disk during local wrangler dev by reading it with the Node.js compat flag. Simplest correct approach: serve it via a static route that reads the file path relative to the worker — wrangler dev serves from the local filesystem. Use: import widgetJs from '../../widget/dist/pluggable-bot.js' with assert { type: 'text' } NOT supported on Workers; instead declare a WASM/text binding in wrangler.toml. CORRECT approach: add to wrangler.toml: [[rules]] type='Text' globs=['**/*.js'] and set main. Actually simplest: use the wrangler 'assets' feature or read the file manually. DEFINITIVE approach chosen: in packages/server/wrangler.toml add a [text_blob] binding: WIDGET_JS = '../../widget/dist/pluggable-bot.js'. In src/index.ts access c.env.WIDGET_JS. Update tsconfig Bindings type accordingly.
steps: Implement packages/server/src/types.ts — export interfaces: Message { role: 'user'|'assistant'|'system'; content: string; }. PageContext { url: string; title: string; visibleText: string; }. KnowledgeChunk { id: string; title: string; content: string; url: string; score?: number; }. ChatRequest { message: string; pageContext: PageContext; history: Message[]; }. TrainRequest { url?: string; content?: string; title?: string; }. Bindings { OPENAI_API_KEY: string; WIDGET_JS: string; }.

Implement packages/server/src/knowledge.ts — in-memory store: let chunks: KnowledgeChunk[] = []. On module init, try to read data/knowledge.json using fs (only available under wrangler dev with nodejs_compat). Wrap in try/catch — if it fails (Workers prod), start empty. Export: addChunks(newChunks: KnowledgeChunk[]): void — pushes to chunks array; tries to write JSON to data/knowledge.json (ignore errors in prod). search(query: string, topK = 5): KnowledgeChunk[] — tokenize query (lowercase split on non-word), score each chunk using TF-IDF: for each chunk compute term frequency of query tokens in chunk.content, multiply by log(1 + N / (1 + df)) where N = total chunks and df = chunks containing the term. Return top topK by score with score field set. splitIntoChunks(content: string, title: string, url: string): KnowledgeChunk[] — splits content into ~500 char chunks with 50 char overlap, assigns sequential ids, returns array.

Implement packages/server/src/train.ts — export function trainRoute(app: Hono<{Bindings: Bindings}>): void. Calls app.post('/api/train', async (c) => { const body = await c.req.json<TrainRequest>(); const content = body.content ?? ''; const title = body.title ?? body.url ?? 'Untitled'; const url = body.url ?? ''; if (!content.trim()) return c.json({ error: 'content required' }, 400); const newChunks = splitIntoChunks(content, title, url); addChunks(newChunks); return c.json({ chunksAdded: newChunks.length, total: chunks.length }); }). Export chunks array getter for use in index if needed.

Implement packages/server/src/chat.ts — export function chatRoute(app: Hono<{Bindings: Bindings}>): void. Handler logic: (1) parse ChatRequest from request body. (2) call search(message, 5) to get context chunks. (3) build system prompt: 'You are a helpful assistant for the website {pageContext.url}. Use the following knowledge base excerpts to answer questions. If the answer is not in the knowledge base, say so. Knowledge base: {chunks.map(c=>c.content).join(
---
)}'. (4) build messages array: [{role:'system',content:systemPrompt}, ...history.slice(-10), {role:'user',content: message + '

[Page: '+pageContext.title+' '+pageContext.url+']'}]. (5) Check apiKey = c.env.OPENAI_API_KEY. (6a) If apiKey: create OpenAI client with apiKey; call openai.chat.completions.create({ model:'gpt-4o-mini', messages, stream:true }). Return SSE Response with ReadableStream that iterates stream, enqueues data:{token} lines, ends with data:[DONE]. (6b) If no apiKey: build mockResponse string = 'I am a demo bot (no OpenAI API key configured). You asked: ' + message + '. Based on the knowledge base I found ' + chunks.length + ' relevant chunks. To enable real AI responses, set OPENAI_API_KEY in .dev.vars.'. Stream it word by word with 50ms delay using ReadableStream. (7) Both paths set headers: Content-Type:text/event-stream, Cache-Control:no-cache, Access-Control-Allow-Origin:*.

Implement packages/server/src/index.ts — create Hono app typed as Hono<{Bindings:Bindings}>. Add cors() middleware from 'hono/cors'. Register chatRoute(app) and trainRoute(app). Add /api/health. Add /widget/pluggable-bot.js route returning c.env.WIDGET_JS as application/javascript. Add / route returning a demo HTML string. Export default app.

Update packages/server/wrangler.toml to add the text_blob binding: after the [vars] section add: [[rules]] { type = 'Text', globs = ['**/*.js'] }. Actually use the correct wrangler text_blob syntax: [text_blobs] WIDGET_JS = '../../widget/dist/pluggable-bot.js'. This tells wrangler to read that file and expose it as a string in env.WIDGET_JS.
Update packages/server/tsconfig.json Bindings type: ensure the Bindings interface in types.ts has WIDGET_JS: string. No tsconfig change needed if types are already correct.

Create demo/index.html — standalone page that: (1) has realistic sample content about a fictional SaaS product 'Acme Analytics' with features, pricing (Free/$29/$99), FAQ (3 questions), and a contact section, (2) includes <script src='http://localhost:8787/widget/pluggable-bot.js' data-api-url='http://localhost:8787' data-bot-name='Acme Bot' data-primary-color='#4f46e5'></script>, (3) has a sticky 'Train Bot on This Page' button (top-right) that on click does fetch('http://localhost:8787/api/train', {method:'POST',headers:{'Content-Type':'application/json'},body:JSON.stringify({url:location.href,title:document.title,content:document.body.innerText})}).then(r=>r.json()).then(d=>alert('Trained! Added '+d.chunksAdded+' chunks.')), (4) clean modern styling with CSS variables.

Create README.md at repo root with sections: ## Quick Start (prereqs Node 18+, clone, npm install, npm run build -w packages/widget, optionally create packages/server/.dev.vars with OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-..., npm run dev — opens on http://localhost:8787), ## Embed on Any Website (copy-paste script tag), ## Training Your Bot (curl example and Train button), ## Configuration (data-* attribute table), ## Architecture (brief description of widget+server+SSE pattern), ## Development (wrangler dev, esbuild watch commands).

Run end-to-end verification: (1) cd packages/server && npx tsc --noEmit (exits 0). (2) npm run dev -w packages/server (wrangler dev starts on port 8787 — check output for 'Ready on http://localhost:8787'). Manual check: open browser to http://localhost:8787 — demo page loads; widget launcher appears bottom-right; clicking sends a message and receives streaming mock response.

curl -X POST http://localhost:8787/api/train -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"content":"Acme Analytics pricing: Free plan, Pro $29/mo","title":"Pricing"}' — returns {"chunksAdded":1}

findings: INTEGRATION VERIFIED (Iteration 1). Fix applied: replaced new Function('m','return import(m)') in knowledge.ts with direct import('node:fs/promises') using @ts-ignore — the Workers runtime (workerd) blocks new Function() as code-generation-from-strings, causing an EvalError that prevented wrangler dev from starting. Also added compatibility_flags = ["nodejs_compat"] to wrangler.toml to enable node:fs/promises under wrangler dev. Evidence: (1) npm run build -w packages/widget exits 0 — dist/pluggable-bot.js is 8.6 KB raw (well under 30 KB gzip). (2) npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/widget/tsconfig.json exits 0. (3) npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/server/tsconfig.json exits 0. (4) wrangler dev starts and prints 'Ready on http://127.0.0.1:8787'. (5) GET /api/health => {"status":"ok","chunks":0} HTTP 200. (6) GET /widget/pluggable-bot.js => HTTP 200, 8796 bytes of JavaScript. (7) POST /api/train with content=Acme pricing => {"chunksAdded":1,"total":1}. (8) POST /api/chat => SSE stream with word tokens and final data: [DONE] line. (9) GET / => HTTP 200, 10763 bytes HTML containing Acme Analytics and widget embed. (10) demo/index.html and README.md both exist.
